title: The `KEGGemUP` package: building KEGG pathway graphs and mapping real data results
text: first step installing package. dont package installed can running: load . KEGG pathways used many bioinformatics contexts, package package can make easy implement analysis real data. important part bioinformatics analyses data integration visiazionation. KEGGemUP aims facilitate tasks providing functions parse KEGG pathways build graph objects, idea use graph map thre results differential expression analyses. KEGG database uses pathway ids identify pathway, example “hsa00563” KEGG pathway ID “Glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchor biosynthesis” humans. can use pathway IDs download KGML files pathway parse build graph objects. id must organism prefix, example “hsa” human pathways, “mmu” mouse pathways, etc. vignette assumes already performed differential expression analysis results available data.frame (can easily obtain edgeR limma running .data.frame() table results object). reproduce situation now build example differential expression result using macrophage dataset macrophage package: bioconductor page learn graph manipulation can refer igraph visNetwork documentation: igraph package creating manipulating graphs R. visNetwork package interactive visualization graphs R, R interface javascript library vis.js.
code: install.packages("remotes")      remotes::install_github("edo98811/KEGGemUP") library("KEGGemUP") message("--- Loading packages...") #> --- Loading packages...  suppressPackageStartupMessages({   library("macrophage")   library("org.Hs.eg.db")   library("SummarizedExperiment")   library("AnnotationDbi")   library("clusterProfiler")   library("limma")   library("edgeR") }) message("- Done!") #> - Done!  # Load the macrophage dataset --------------------------------------------------- data(gse) rownames(gse) <- substr(rownames(gse), 1, 15)  # truncate rownames at 15 characters  # limma analysis --------------------------------------------------------------- condition <- factor(colData(gse)[, "condition_name"]) design <- model.matrix(~0 + condition)  contrast.matrix <- makeContrasts(   IFNg_vs_naive = conditionIFNg - conditionnaive,   levels = design )  dge <- DGEList(assay(gse)) dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)  cutoff <- 1 drop <- which(apply(cpm(dge), 1, max) < cutoff) dge <- dge[-drop, ]  voom_mat <- voom(dge, design, plot = FALSE) fit <- lmFit(voom_mat, design) fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrast.matrix) fit2 <- eBayes(fit2)  # Empirical Bayes moderation  # Gene annotation ---------------------------------------------------------------  anns <- AnnotationDbi::select(   org.Hs.eg.db,   keys = rownames(gse),   columns = c("SYMBOL", "ENTREZID"),   keytype = "ENSEMBL",   multiVals = "first" ) #> 'select()' returned 1:many mapping between keys and columns  # limma results --------------------------------------------------------------- res_macrophage_IFNg_vs_naive_limma <- topTable(   fit2,   coef = "IFNg_vs_naive",   adjust = "fdr",   number = Inf,   confint = TRUE )  res_macrophage_IFNg_vs_naive_limma$ENTREZID <- anns$ENTREZID[match(rownames(res_macrophage_IFNg_vs_naive_limma), anns$ENSEMBL)]  # Enrichment analysis ---------------------------------------------------------- de_entrez_IFNg_vs_naive_genes <- anns $ENTREZID[   (!is.na(res_macrophage_IFNg_vs_naive_limma$adj.P.Val)) &     (res_macrophage_IFNg_vs_naive_limma$adj.P.Valj <= 0.05) ]

text: map differential expression results nodes KEGG pathway graph can use map_results_to_nodes(). input function graph object built kegg_to_graph() list differential expression results tables single differential expression results table. can also pass input map_results_to_nodes() single data.frame differential expression results. dataframe must contain least two columns: one KEGG feature IDs (without organism prefix) another values map nodes (e.g., log2 fold changes). can pass function names columns differ default ones parameters feature_column value_column. Note KEGG IDs without organism prefix ENTREZ IDs genes. feature types (e.g., compounds) need make sure IDs differential expression results table match KEGG IDs used graph. defualt parameters : feature_column: “KEGG_ids” value_column: “log2FoldChange” multiple differential expression results tables (example one metabolomics one transcriptomics) map nodes can pass list lists. sublist must contain following elements: de_table: data.frame differential expression results. value_column: name column de_table containing values map nodes. feature_column: name column de_table containing feature IDs (e.g., ENTREZ IDs) correspond KEGG ids graph (without organism prefix). example build list differential expression results tables. case one element, ideally one omics layer source want map graph nodes.

title: Parse KEGG KGML files to extract nodes data frame. — parse_kgml_entries
text: data.frame following columns: id Unique identifier entry within KGML pathway (id attribute). kegg_name KEGG-specific name identifier entity (name attribute). may include one KEGG identifiers gene IDs, compound IDs, enzyme EC numbers. Preceded organism ID type Type node (type attribute), indicating biological entity class 'gene', 'enzyme', 'compound', 'map', 'ortholog', 'group'. link URL linking KEGG resource entry, available (link attribute). reaction Associated reaction ID(s), (reaction attribute). Typically present enzyme entries. graphics_name Display name entry, taken name attribute <graphics> node. label Text label visualization purposes. fgcolor Foreground color graphical element (fgcolor attribute <graphics>). bgcolor Background color graphical element (bgcolor attribute <graphics>). graphics_type Shape representation type graphical element (type attribute <graphics>), 'rectangle', 'circle', 'line'. x X-coordinate node’s position pathway diagram (x attribute <graphics>). y Y-coordinate node’s position pathway diagram (y attribute <graphics>). width Width graphical element (width attribute <graphics>). height Height graphical element (height attribute <graphics>).

title: Parse KEGG KGML files to extract nodes data frame. — parse_kgml_entries
text: function parses KEGG KGML (KEGG Markup Language) XML file extracts <entry> elements, representing biological entity KEGG pathway diagram. node may contain nested <graphics> elements defining visual properties (position, size, colors) <component> elements define group membership composite entities. resulting data provides tidy, one-row-per-entry representation suitable integration relational data models network visualization frameworks (e.g., igraphor visNetwork).

title: Parse KEGG KGML files to extract relations and edges data frames. — parse_kgml_relations
text: function reads KEGG KGML (KEGG Markup Language) file, encodes pathway information XML, extracts <relation> elements describe interactions relationships entities pathway. <relation> may contain one <relation_subtype> elements provide additional details interaction. result tidy data.frame suitable network analysis visualization, row represents one relation–relation_subtype pair.
